situation: A first-year student tells her friend she has already finished her essay. In fact, she has not started it yet.

situation: A chemistry professor announces that the exam will be in this room tomorrow morning. Several students look worried and write it down.
A new exchange student asks where she can find the faculty office. The man at the counter points to the wrong building.

place: a group study room in Seoul
situation: A strict project leader tells his team to bring their laptops and to sit in the front row. Nobody asks why.
An older roommate warns the new student not to leave food on the windowsill. The local pigeons are very fast.

place: a student club meeting in Cape Town
situation: The club treasurer admits he spent the party budget on snacks for himself. He promises to return the money.

place: a corridor of a music school in Vienna
situation: Two violin students whisper that the head of the school is going to retire next year. They heard it from the cleaner.
The IT assistant says students must not eat in the lab and should save their work every ten minutes.
At the party, a graduate tells how he once slept through his final alarm and ran to the exam in his pyjamas.
A research student says the lab is closed on Mondays. It has been closed on Mondays for years.

place: a furniture shop office in Stockholm
situation: The sales manager says the delivery will arrive here next Tuesday at nine. Nobody checks the calendar.
A new accountant asks if anyone knows the Wi-Fi password. The whole office answers with three different words at once.
A tired editor tells the young reporter to cut the article in half and to use shorter sentences. The reporter looks at his phone.

place: a shared office kitchen in Amsterdam
situation: A friendly colleague warns the new hire that the coffee machine is broken on Fridays. It makes hot water instead.
The team supervisor admits he forgot to book the meeting room, but he refuses to move the meeting to Monday.
Two cashiers pass on a rumour that the branch will close at the end of the year. The manager has said nothing about it.

place: a taxi company office in Jakarta
situation: The dispatcher says drivers must turn off their radios at night and should not park in front of the office.

place: a design studio in Mexico City
situation: A graphic designer tells how he once printed a poster backwards and the client loved it and ordered more.
The receptionist says the office has no elevator. The building is old and still has no elevator.

place: a job interview in a bakery in Lyon
situation: A nervous applicant says she has worked in a bakery for two years. Her last job was actually at a petrol station.

situation: The manager tells the new drivers that training starts here at seven tomorrow. Two of them arrive at the wrong building.
A young cook asks if the restaurant is open on Sundays. The owner asks why he wants to know so soon.
A floor supervisor tells the temporary workers to put the boxes by the door and to sign the sheet before leaving.

place: a hair salon in Tel Aviv
situation: A senior stylist warns the new apprentice never to leave scissors in water overnight. They rust very fast.
A recruiter promises to call every candidate by Friday, then admits he lost half of the forms on the train.
Two nurses pass on a rumour that the hospital will hire twenty new staff in the spring. Nobody has seen an official notice.
A new team leader says employees may take two short breaks but must stay near their desks.

place: a hotel training room in Bangkok
situation: An experienced receptionist tells how she once welcomed a guest by the wrong name for a whole week and he never corrected her.
A mechanic tells the new helper that the garage closes at noon on Saturdays. It has been like that for thirty years.

place: an online shop office in Krakow
situation: A customer service agent says the warehouse has already sent the parcel. The tracking page shows it is still in the box.

situation: A shop assistant tells a customer that the sale ends here on Sunday and there will be no new sizes until next month.
An elderly shopper asks if the tomatoes are from the local farm or from the big city market. The seller looks at the sky and says nothing.
A young assistant asks the delivery man to leave the boxes at the back door and to ring the bell twice.
An experienced seller warns a mother not to buy the white shoes because they get dirty in one afternoon.
The manager promises a refund for the broken phone, then refuses to give it because the customer lost the receipt.
Two shop owners pass on a rumour that a new big store will open on the top floor. The centre has no top floor.
A pharmacist says customers must show a photo ID for some medicines and should keep them away from children.
A delivery driver tells how he once took a hundred roses to the wrong wedding and the bride still thanked him.

situation: A station worker says the last train to the city leaves here in five minutes. Two tourists run the wrong way.
A lost traveller asks if this ferry goes to the island with the blue church. The captain smiles and says there are seven such islands.

place: a plane cabin over the ocean
situation: A flight attendant asks passengers to put their seats up and to turn off all phones before landing.
An old driver warns the passengers to keep their tickets in a safe pocket and to watch their bags on the night bus.
The hotel manager promises a room with a sea view, then admits the only free room looks at the car park.
Two passengers at the airport cafe pass on a rumour that all flights to London are cancelled because of fog. The board says nothing yet.

place: a ferry on the Baltic Sea
situation: A crew member says passengers must wear life jackets during the drill and may not go on the top deck in a storm.
A hiker tells how she once took the wrong bus to the mountains and ended up in a village with no road back for two days.

place: a border crossing between two countries
situation: A guard says the crossing is closed at night. It has been closed at night for as long as anyone remembers.
